title: Private deployments: VPC & On-Prem - Deployment Guide, Reference Architectures, Day-2 Ops, Upgrades and Customer Requirements Library
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical engineering and customer-facing guide for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It consolidates: reference architectures, packaging and installation notes, day-2 operational procedures, upgrade and rollback playbooks, and a customer requirements library (network, security, capacity, and compliance). Use this guide for pre-sales scoping, implementation, and operational handover.

Scope and intended audience

- Scope: All private deployment modes supported by Redwood (VPC-hosted private control plane, customer-managed VPC, and full on-prem appliance/air-gapped installations).
- Audience: Solutions Engineers, Customer Site Reliability Engineers, Platform Engineers, Security/Compliance reviewers, and Professional Services.

High-level deployment patterns

1) VPC-managed (recommended for cloud customers)
   - Redwood control plane in our hosted environment; data plane lives in customer VPC.
   - Use-case: customers who need network isolation, KMS integration, and easy autoscaling.

2) Private control plane (hybrid)
   - Customer hosts control plane components in their cloud account; Redwood provides orchestration tooling and monitoring integrations.
   - Use-case: customers with strict residency rules or shared responsibility preferences.

3) On-prem / air-gapped
   - Full stack delivered as packages/containers and optional appliance image for isolated environments.
   - Use-case: regulated industries or customers that cannot accept outbound network connections.

Reference architectures

Below are the three validated reference architectures and typical sizing guidance. For each architecture, see the diagram links in Related pages.

- Small (PoC / evaluation)
  - 2 control-plane VMs (2 vCPU, 8GB) for admin APIs and telemetry proxy
  - 1 gateway VM + 1 GPU worker (NVIDIA T4 or equivalent)
  - Storage: 200GB for logs/KV cache
  - Networking: Single private subnet, NAT for outbound updates if allowed

- Production (multi-zone)
  - Control plane: 3x VMs for HA (4 vCPU, 16GB), behind internal LB
  - GPU pool: min 3 worker nodes (A100/RTX6000 or equivalent) with autoscaling group
  - Redis/KV cache cluster (3 nodes), object store (S3/RadosGW) for model artifacts
  - Metrics & tracing: Prometheus + Tempo in customer account or via secure proxy

- On-prem appliance (air-gapped)
  - Appliance: 2x management nodes (HA) + N GPU servers per cluster node (per customer sizing)
  - Local object store (Ceph/Rook) or network storage with replication
  - Local KMS or HSM integration guidance provided in the packaging section

Prerequisites and customer requirements (summary table)

| Category | Minimum requirement | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Network | Private VPC/subnet; 2x /24s | Separate control & data subnets | Ports: 443, 50051, 22 (ops only) |
| IPs | 6 static IPs (small) | Dedicated elastic IPs for gateways |
| Compute | 1 GPU worker (PoC) | GPU type per workload (A100 recommended) | See model sizing appendix |
| Storage | 200GB persisted | S3-compatible object store + 1TB cache | Use encryption-at-rest |
| Identity | Service account with least privilege | SAML/SCIM for users, KMS access | RBAC mapping required |
| Compliance | SOC2 / ISO evidence requested | Optional integration with customer SIEM | Upload audit logs to central SIEM |

Note: full, downloadable customer requirements worksheet is available as CSV from the Solutions Engineering toolkit (internal link).

On-prem packaging and installation

Packaging formats
- Container images (OCI) hosted in a customer-accessible registry (for VPC/hybrid).
- Tarball/air-gap bundle with images + manifest + install scripts for isolated installs.
- Appliance VM image (OVA) for customers who want hypervisor-based delivery.

Installation modes
1. Automated (recommended) - install.sh or terraform module
   - install.sh --mode=airgap --bundle /tmp/redwood-bundle.tar.gz --kubeconfig /root/.kube/config
   - Uses systemd units in the appliance for lifecycle management
2. Kubernetes helm chart - for cloud and on-prem K8s clusters
   - helm repo add redwood https://helm.redwood.ai/charts
   - helm upgrade --install redwood redwood/platform -f values-production.yaml
3. Manual (support-only) - unpack bundle and run components in order (control plane -> gateway -> workers)

Packaging checklist (pre-installation)
- Confirm networking and firewall rules (ports & CIDRs)
- Ensure KMS credentials and service account keys are staged
- Verify registry access (or transfer air-gap bundle)
- Confirm model artifact storage and credentials configured

Deployment steps: VPC (canonical, numbered)

1. Provision networking: control-subnet, data-subnet, NAT & route tables.
2. Create service accounts & KMS keys; grant least privilege roles.
3. Deploy control plane: configure internal load balancer and DNS entries.
4. Deploy gateway(s) with public ingress or private endpoint per customer policy.
5. Register GPU workers with the control plane; verify health checks and KV cache connectivity.
6. Install monitoring agent and verify metrics ingestion.
7. Run validation suite: connectivity, model load, inference smoke tests, latency checks.
8. Handover operational runbook and access to on-call rotations.

Day-2 operations (runbooks & playbooks)

Common procedures (quick index)
- Scaling workers up/down (manual + autoscaler rules)
- Replacing a failed GPU node
- Troubleshooting model load failures
- KV cache warm/cold state recovery
- Recovering telemetry pipeline (Prometheus/Tempo)

Example: Replace a failed GPU worker (playbook)
1. Identify failed node via alert or /health endpoint.
2. Drain traffic from node: curl -XPOST https://control-plane.local/api/v1/nodes/<node>/drain
3. Remove node from autoscaling group or mark as unhealthy in LB.
4. Provision replacement node using the same AMI/container image and bootstrap config.
5. Register node with control plane and wait for warm-up: expected warm-up 3-6 minutes for model KV cache.
6. Verify inference correctness with 5 smoke sample requests.
7. Close incident and record in post-incident log.

Upgrade and rollback procedures

Principles
- Always perform upgrades in canary -> staged -> full rollout order.
- Keep model-serving compatibility matrices for kernel/quantization combinations.
- Maintain automated runbook tasks to validate quality regressions (prompts + evals).

Canary upgrade steps
1. Create release artifact and publish to registry (or prepare air-gap bundle).
2. Deploy to single gateway and a single worker in a canary pool.
3. Run smoke tests, latency/throughput benchmarks, and evals against the canary.
4. If metrics pass, promote to 20% traffic for 2 hours and re-evaluate.
5. Continue staged promotion (50% -> 100%) with automated rollback triggers on SLO breaches.

Automated rollback triggers
- 5xx rate increase > 1% over baseline sustained for 10 minutes
- 95th percentile latency increase > 30% vs baseline for 30 minutes
- Quality regression alerts from the eval harness (prompt set failure rate delta > 3%)

Manual rollback steps (if automation fails)
1. Pause rollout and TTL autoscaling for the affected pools.
2. Re-deploy previous artifact to the affected nodes using the same mechanism (helm/tarball).
3. Repoint traffic via feature flags or LB to the previous version.
4. Run smoke tests and notify stakeholders in the incident channel.

Customer requirements library (detailed checklist)

For each customer engagement collect and validate the following items. Use the Customer Requirements Worksheet to capture values.

- Network & routing
  - Control plane CIDRs and allowed egress CIDRs
  - NAT gateway / proxy requirements
  - TLS interception policies (certificate pinning notes)
- Identity & access
  - Service account roles and policies
  - SAML/SCIM metadata for SSO integration
  - KMS/HSM access model and key rotation schedule
- Security & compliance
  - Required certifications (SOC2, ISO, PCI as applicable)
  - Audit log retention period and SIEM integration details
  - Data residency constraints and model artifact residency
- Capacity & performance
  - Expected QPS and peak concurrency by region
  - Model catalog and avg token length distribution
  - Target latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and throughput SLOs
- Operational contacts & SLAs
  - Oncall rotation and escalation path
  - Scheduled maintenance windows and blackout windows

Configuration matrix (sample entries)

| Field | Example value | Owner | Required |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Control plane subnet CIDR | 10.1.0.0/24 | Customer networking | true |
| Gateway public IP | 34.120.45.9 | Customer networking | false |
| KMS key ID | projects/prod/keys/redwood-123 | Customer security | true |
| GPU type | NVIDIA A100 | Customer infra | true |
| Object store endpoint | https://s3.example.com | Customer infra | true |

Operational dashboards, SLOs and alert thresholds

- SLOs (default for private deployments):
  - Latency p95 < 150ms for small models; p95 < 500ms for long context/large models
  - Error rate < 0.5%
  - Uptime 99.9% (control plane)
- Key alerts: high 5xx rate, worker registration failures, KV cache misses spike, model load timeouts, disk pressure > 80%

Ownership & escalation

- Owner: eng-private-deployments team (primary). Operational contacts: Solutions Engineering (pre-sales) and Customer Success (handover).
- Escalation path: oncall infra -> eng-platform -> eng-sre -> eng-serving-runtime (model/kernel issues)

Appendix: Validation checklist (pre-handover)

1. All nodes registered and healthy in control plane.
2. Prometheus metrics present and dashboards reporting within expected ranges.
3. 10 sample inference requests pass end-to-end validation.
4. Audit logs flowing to customer SIEM or Redwood secure log proxy.
5. Oncall runbook reviewed with customer SRE and signed off.
